models.name: article_categories
models.description:
Article category reference data that organizes discussion board content into logical topic areas.

Every article published on the discussion board must belong to exactly one category from this predefined set. Categories provide the primary organizational structure enabling users to browse articles by topic area. The system maintains a fixed set of categories rather than allowing unlimited user-created categories, ensuring consistent content organization and preventing category fragmentation.

Categories include metadata describing their purpose, character limits for article content within the category, and validity status. Soft deletion is supported to maintain data integrity when categories are deprecated while preserving the ability to reference them from historical articles.

Related entities: discussion_board_articles references this table via category_id when articles are created or updated.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Unique machine-readable identifier for the category (e.g., 'economic-policy', 'political-governance'). Used in APIs and internal references. Must be 5-50 lowercase alphanumeric characters with hyphens.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Human-readable display name for the category (e.g., 'Economic Policy', 'Political Governance'). Shown in user interfaces, category listings, and article filters. 10-100 characters.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation of the category scope and purpose. Helps users understand which category their article should belong to. Maximum 500 characters. Examples: 'Articles about taxation, trade, regulation, and economic policy decisions' for Economic Policy category.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Numeric order for displaying categories in user interfaces. Lower numbers appear first in category menus and navigation. Defaults to 0. Used by sort order when displaying category lists.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether this category is currently available for article submission. Active categories appear in category selection dropdowns when users create articles. Inactive categories persist for historical reference but prevent new articles from being assigned. Defaults to true.

plainFields.name: article_count
plainFields.description: Denormalized count of published articles in this category. Used for display purposes (e.g., 'Economic Policy (47 articles'). Updated when articles are published or unpublished. Defaults to 0. Should be recalculated periodically for accuracy.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was created. ISO 8601 format. Set automatically on record creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was last modified. ISO 8601 format. Updated whenever any field changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was soft-deleted (made inactive). ISO 8601 format. Null for active categories. Soft deletion preserves historical category data while removing the category from active use.

models.name: content_guidelines
models.description:
Content policy rules and moderation guidelines that define community standards for articles and comments.

The content guidelines table stores the authoritative rules that moderators enforce when reviewing articles and monitoring comments. Each guideline entry specifies a policy rule, whether it applies to articles or comments, the severity level if violated, and examples to help moderators make consistent decisions.

Guidelines are organized by policy area (hate speech, misinformation, spam, off-topic, etc.) and include detailed descriptions of prohibited behavior. The system maintains the complete set of active guidelines for reference by moderators and contributors. Soft deletion is supported to preserve historical policy changes while maintaining audit trails of previous guidelines.

Moderation decisions reference specific guidelines when removing content or issuing warnings, creating accountability and transparency about why content was removed.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Machine-readable identifier for the guideline (e.g., 'hate-speech', 'misinformation', 'spam'). 5-50 lowercase alphanumeric characters with hyphens. Used in moderation logs and audit trails.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Short, descriptive title of the guideline (e.g., 'Hate Speech', 'Misinformation', 'Commercial Spam'). 10-100 characters. Displayed in moderation dashboards and violation notices.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation of the policy and what content violates it. Should include clear examples of prohibited behavior and the rationale for the policy. Maximum 2000 characters. Moderators use this when making judgment calls about borderline content.

plainFields.name: applies_to_articles
plainFields.description: Whether this guideline applies to article content. If true, moderators review articles against this guideline during approval. Defaults to true for most guidelines.

plainFields.name: applies_to_comments
plainFields.description: Whether this guideline applies to comment content. If true, moderators monitor comments for violations of this guideline. Defaults to true for most guidelines.

plainFields.name: severity_level
plainFields.description: Classification of violation severity: 'minor' (edit/warning), 'moderate' (removal/warning), 'severe' (removal/suspension). Guides moderator response proportionality. Severity level informs escalation decisions.

plainFields.name: violation_consequence
plainFields.description: Description of typical consequences for violating this guideline (e.g., 'comment removal', 'article rejection with feedback', 'account suspension after 3 violations'). Maximum 500 characters. Helps set contributor expectations.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Numeric order for displaying guidelines in user-facing policy documentation. Lower numbers appear first. Defaults to 0. Used to organize guidelines by importance or category.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether this guideline is currently enforced. Active guidelines are displayed in policy documentation and used by moderators. Inactive guidelines are retained for historical reference but not actively enforced. Defaults to true.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guideline was created. ISO 8601 format. Marks when the policy rule was first established.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guideline was last modified. ISO 8601 format. Updated when policy descriptions or enforcement rules change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guideline was soft-deleted or made inactive. ISO 8601 format. Null for active guidelines. Soft deletion preserves historical audit trail of policy changes.

models.name: system_configurations
models.description:
Application-wide configuration settings and system parameters that control platform behavior.

The system configurations table stores site-wide settings and operational parameters that control how the discussion board functions. Settings include password requirements, session timeouts, rate limits, file upload constraints, and feature flags that determine which features are enabled.

Configuration entries use a key-value structure with a configuration key (e.g., 'password_min_length', 'session_timeout_minutes', 'file_upload_max_size_mb') and corresponding value. Each setting includes a description explaining its purpose and impact on the system.

Administrators manage system configurations to tune platform behavior without requiring code changes. Changes to configurations take effect immediately or after specified cache expiration periods. All configuration changes are audited with timestamps for accountability.

plainFields.name: config_key
plainFields.description: Unique machine-readable identifier for the configuration setting (e.g., 'password_min_length', 'session_timeout_minutes', 'file_upload_max_size_mb'). 10-100 lowercase alphanumeric characters with underscores. Used as primary lookup key for retrieving configuration values.

plainFields.name: config_value
plainFields.description: The actual configuration value as a string (e.g., '8' for password_min_length, '30' for session_timeout_minutes). Values are stored as strings and should be parsed to appropriate types (int, boolean, etc.) by application code. Maximum 5000 characters for complex values like policy text.

plainFields.name: config_type
plainFields.description: Data type classification for the configuration value: 'string', 'integer', 'boolean', 'decimal', 'json'. Indicates how the config_value should be parsed by the application. Helps validate configuration values.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Explanation of what this configuration controls and why it matters. Examples: 'Minimum number of characters required for user passwords', 'Session timeout in minutes after which users must re-authenticate', 'Maximum file size in MB for article attachments'. Maximum 1000 characters.

plainFields.name: is_modifiable
plainFields.description: Whether administrators can modify this configuration through the admin interface. Some core settings (like schema version) are read-only and marked as false to prevent accidental changes. Defaults to true for most settings.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the configuration setting was created. ISO 8601 format. Marks when this setting was first established.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the configuration value was last modified. ISO 8601 format. Updated whenever an administrator changes the configuration value.

models.name: discussion_board_contributors
models.description:
Registered contributor user accounts for the discussion board.

Stores authentication credentials, profile information, and account status for contributors who can create articles and post comments. Each contributor account is unique by email and username. Soft deletion preserves contributor information while enabling account recovery within 6 months.

Password security is enforced through bcrypt hashing with minimum 12 salt rounds. Email addresses are stored plaintext for authentication flows (login, password reset, notifications) but should be treated as sensitive data. Account creation requires email verification before enabling login.

Contributors maintain separate session management from moderators, requiring dedicated session tables for security isolation. Violation history and account restrictions track contributor standing and enforcement actions.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address used for authentication and account recovery. Must be unique across all contributor accounts. Valid email format required (user@domain.com).

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Bcrypt-hashed password with minimum 12 salt rounds. Password must be at least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character. Never stores plaintext password.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: Public display name for articles and comments. Must be unique across all contributors. 3-50 characters, alphanumeric and underscore only. Immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Whether the contributor's email address has been verified through confirmation link. False until verification email is clicked. Account cannot post articles or comments until verified.

plainFields.name: account_status
plainFields.description: Current account status. Valid values: 'active' (normal operation), 'suspended' (temporary ban), 'restricted' (limited posting), 'deleted' (marked for deletion but retained for audit). Defaults to 'active' on creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the contributor account was created in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent account modification. Updated when email, username, password, or status changes. Not updated on session creation or article/comment posting.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when contributor account was deleted (soft delete). Null for active accounts. Retained for 6 months to enable recovery; after 6 months, account and associated data can be permanently purged.

plainFields.name: last_login_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful login. Null if account has never been logged in. Updated only on successful authentication, not on failed attempts.

plainFields.name: password_changed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent password change. Null if password has never been changed from initial setup. All active sessions are invalidated when password changes.

models.name: discussion_board_contributor_sessions
models.description:
Session management for authenticated contributors.

Tracks active sessions for contributor authentication. Each session represents a login instance with connection context (IP address, referrer URL, accessed URL). Sessions enforce 30-minute access token expiration and 7-day refresh token expiration.

One contributor can have multiple concurrent sessions from different devices or browsers. Sessions are created on successful login and invalidated on logout or password change. Connection metadata (IP, referrer) enables security monitoring and abuse detection.

Sessions follow the mandatory specification with required fields: ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at. No additional fields beyond this specification are allowed.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_contributor_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the contributor account. Multiple concurrent sessions allowed per contributor.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the session connection. Used for security monitoring and abuse detection. IPv4 or IPv6 format.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL of the page where session was initiated (connection URL). Enables tracking of session origination context.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP Referrer header value from session creation request. Indicates where user came from before logging in.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when session was created in ISO 8601 format. Marks the login time.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when session was explicitly terminated (logout). Null for active sessions. Session is also implicitly expired after 7 days of creation.

models.name: discussion_board_moderators
models.description:
Moderator accounts with elevated administrative permissions.

Stores authentication and profile information for moderators who review articles, manage comments, and enforce community standards. Moderators are a distinct user type from contributors, with separate account management and session handling.

Each moderator account is unique by email and username. Moderators require email verification and maintain separate session table for security isolation from regular contributors. All moderators have identical permissions; role differentiation is not supported (all moderators have equal authority).

Moderation authority is recorded through audit logs that track which moderator performed each action. Account status tracks moderator availability (active, suspended, deleted). Moderators retain full contributor capabilities (can create articles, post comments) while also accessing moderation tools.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address used for moderator authentication and account recovery. Must be unique across all moderator accounts. Valid email format required (user@domain.com).

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Bcrypt-hashed password with minimum 12 salt rounds. Password must be at least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character. Never stores plaintext password.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: Public display name for moderation actions and audit trail. Must be unique across all moderators. 3-50 characters, alphanumeric and underscore only. Immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Whether the moderator's email address has been verified through confirmation link. False until verification email is clicked. Account cannot access moderation tools until verified.

plainFields.name: account_status
plainFields.description: Current account status. Valid values: 'active' (normal operation), 'suspended' (temporary ban from moderation), 'deleted' (marked for deletion). Defaults to 'active' on creation.

plainFields.name: moderation_tier
plainFields.description: Moderator permission level. Current value: 'full' (all moderation permissions). Reserved for future role differentiation. All moderators currently have identical permissions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was created in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent account modification. Updated when email, username, password, status, or tier changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when moderator account was deleted (soft delete). Null for active accounts. Retained for compliance purposes; moderator actions remain attributed to their ID in audit logs.

plainFields.name: last_login_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful login to moderation dashboard. Null if account has never been logged in.

plainFields.name: password_changed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent password change. Null if password has never been changed. All active sessions are invalidated when password changes.

models.name: discussion_board_moderator_sessions
models.description:
Session management for authenticated moderators.

Tracks active sessions for moderator authentication and access to moderation dashboards. Each session represents a login instance with connection context (IP address, referrer URL, accessed URL). Sessions enforce 30-minute access token expiration and 7-day refresh token expiration.

One moderator can have multiple concurrent sessions from different devices or browsers. Sessions are created on successful moderator login and invalidated on logout or password change. Connection metadata (IP, referrer) enables security monitoring of moderator actions.

Sessions follow the mandatory specification with required fields: ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at. Moderator sessions are separate from contributor sessions for security isolation and access control differentiation.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the moderator account. Multiple concurrent sessions allowed per moderator.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the session connection. Used for security monitoring and audit trail of moderator actions. IPv4 or IPv6 format.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL of the page where session was initiated (connection URL). Enables tracking of where moderator accessed moderation tools.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP Referrer header value from session creation request. Indicates origin of moderator login request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when session was created in ISO 8601 format. Marks the login time for moderation access.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when session was explicitly terminated (logout). Null for active sessions. Session is also implicitly expired after 7 days of creation.

models.name: discussion_board_contributor_violations
models.description:
Violation history tracking for contributors who breach community guidelines.

Records each policy violation (content removal, comment deletion, guideline breach) committed by a contributor. Enables moderation escalation: first violation triggers warning, subsequent violations within 30 days result in restrictions or suspensions.

Each violation entry includes violation type (article removal, comment violation, misinformation, harassment, etc.), severity level (minor, moderate, severe), contributing moderator ID, and recorded timestamp. Violations are never deleted; the complete history is retained for compliance and pattern analysis.

Violation history informs moderator decisions about account restrictions. Multiple violations in short timeframes trigger automatic review recommendations or account suspension escalation. Violations older than 30 days do not count toward escalation, allowing contributors to rehabilitate their standing.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_contributor_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the contributor account that committed the violation. Contributor's {@link discussion_board_contributors.id}.

foreignFields.name: recorded_by_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the moderator who recorded the violation. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}. Null if violation was auto-recorded by system. Optional for system-generated violations.

plainFields.name: violation_type
plainFields.description: Category of the violation. Valid values: 'hate_speech', 'personal_attack', 'misinformation', 'harassment', 'spam', 'explicit_content', 'off_topic', 'platform_abuse', 'other'. Classifies the guideline breached.

plainFields.name: severity_level
plainFields.description: Severity classification of the violation. Valid values: 'minor' (small issue, warning), 'moderate' (clear violation, removal), 'severe' (serious/repeated, restriction/suspension). Guides moderation response.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the violation and context. May reference article ID, comment ID, or other content identifiers. Helps moderators understand violation history. Maximum 1000 characters.

plainFields.name: recorded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the violation was recorded in ISO 8601 format. Marks when moderator identified and recorded the violation.

models.name: discussion_board_account_restrictions
models.description:
Account restrictions and suspensions imposed on contributors by moderators.

Tracks all restrictions applied to contributor accounts as enforcement actions. Restrictions prevent contributors from creating articles or posting comments during the restriction period. Multiple restriction types supported: posting restrictions (3-day, 7-day, custom), temporary suspensions (7-day, 30-day), and permanent bans.

Each restriction records the restriction type, reason, start timestamp, end timestamp (null for active indefinite bans), and moderator who imposed it. Restrictions can be manually lifted by moderators before the scheduled end date. Complete restriction history is retained for compliance and pattern analysis.

Active restrictions (where current time is before end_date or end_date is null) prevent new article submissions and comment posts. Multiple overlapping restrictions are not allowed; applying a new restriction cancels any previous restriction. Contributor notifications include reason for restriction and end date (if applicable).

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_contributor_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the contributor account being restricted. {@link discussion_board_contributors.id}.

foreignFields.name: imposed_by_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the moderator who imposed the restriction. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: restriction_type
plainFields.description: Type of restriction applied. Valid values: 'posting_restriction' (cannot post articles/comments), 'temporary_suspension' (account login denied), 'permanent_ban' (account permanently disabled). Determines enforcement mechanism.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Explanation of why the restriction was imposed. Communicates to contributor why their account was restricted and what conduct led to it. Maximum 500 characters.

plainFields.name: imposed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the restriction was applied in ISO 8601 format. Marks the enforcement action time.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the restriction automatically expires. Null for permanent bans or indefinite restrictions. After this timestamp, restriction is no longer enforced and account returns to normal operation.

plainFields.name: lifted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the restriction was manually lifted by a moderator. Null if restriction expired naturally or is still active. Enables early restriction removal for rehabilitated contributors.

plainFields.name: lifted_by_moderator_id
plainFields.description: Foreign key to the moderator who manually lifted the restriction. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}. Null if restriction was not manually lifted.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Core article entity representing economic and political discussion content created by contributors and published after moderator approval.

Stores complete article metadata including title, content body, author information, publication status, and workflow tracking. Articles progress through a defined lifecycle: draft (author composition) → pending_approval (moderator review) → published (publicly visible) or rejected (awaiting revision).

Supports moderator actions including approval with notes, rejection with feedback, pinning for featured display, and archival. Tracks creation and modification timestamps for audit purposes. Soft deletion preserves article records for compliance while removing public visibility.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_contributor_id
foreignFields.description: Author contributor's {@link discussion_board_contributors.id}. Records the user who originally created the article.

foreignFields.name: article_category_id
foreignFields.description: Category for article organization. References the {@link article_categories.id} for Economics, Politics, or General Discussion topics.

foreignFields.name: approved_by_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator who approved article for publication. References {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}. Null if article not yet approved.

foreignFields.name: last_edited_by_contributor_id
foreignFields.description: Contributor or moderator who last edited the article. References {@link discussion_board_contributors.id}. Null if article never edited after creation.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title displayed in listings and search results. Required field between 5 and 200 characters describing the article topic.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Article body content in plain text or markdown format. Required field between 50 and 50,000 characters containing the main discussion or analysis.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current publication status of the article. Valid values: draft (in progress), pending_approval (awaiting moderator review), published (approved and public), rejected (moderator declined, awaiting revision), archived (removed from listings but searchable), deleted (removed by author or moderator). Determines visibility and editing permissions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when article was originally created by the contributor. Immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of most recent modification to the article. Updates when content, title, category, or status changes.

plainFields.name: published_at
plainFields.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when article was approved and published by moderator. Null if article not yet published. Immutable once set.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when article was deleted by author or moderator. Null if article not deleted. Used for soft deletion to preserve audit trail.

plainFields.name: approval_notes
plainFields.description: Optional moderator feedback provided during article approval. Maximum 1,000 characters. Visible to contributor and other moderators.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Moderator explanation for article rejection. Maximum 500 characters. Provided to contributor to help them understand how to revise the article for resubmission.

plainFields.name: view_count
plainFields.description: Number of times article has been viewed by users. Starts at zero and increments with each article access. Used to identify popular discussions.

plainFields.name: comment_count
plainFields.description: Cached count of published comments on this article. Maintained in sync with actual comment records for display efficiency. Starts at zero.

plainFields.name: is_pinned
plainFields.description: Whether moderator has pinned article to top of listings for featured display. Pinned articles appear before unpinned articles in all browsing and search views. Defaults to false.

plainFields.name: is_locked
plainFields.description: Whether article is locked from further comments and modifications. Locked articles remain visible with existing comments but new comments cannot be posted. Defaults to false.

models.name: discussion_board_article_attachments
models.description:
File attachment metadata for images and documents attached to articles.

Stores information about each file uploaded by contributors to accompany their articles, including original filename, file type, size, upload timestamp, and access URL. Supports up to 10 attachments per article with file size limits (5MB for images, 25MB for documents).

Attachments are managed through their parent article operations. When an article is published, existing attachments remain accessible. When an article is deleted, all associated attachments are removed from storage.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article containing this attachment. References {@link discussion_board_articles.id}. Defines the article context for the file.

foreignFields.name: uploaded_by_contributor_id
foreignFields.description: Contributor who uploaded this attachment. References {@link discussion_board_contributors.id}. Records the uploader for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: Original filename as provided by the uploader. Maximum 255 characters. Displayed to users when downloading or viewing the attachment.

plainFields.name: file_type
plainFields.description: File extension indicating format. Examples: jpg, png, gif, webp, pdf, docx, xlsx, txt. Used for validation and display type determination.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of the file in bytes. Used to enforce size limits (5MB for images, 25MB for documents) and display file size to users.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type for proper browser display and rendering. Examples: image/jpeg, image/png, application/pdf, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document.

plainFields.name: uploaded_at
plainFields.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when file was uploaded. Immutable after upload. Used for audit trail and sorting attachments in display order.

plainFields.name: display_url
plainFields.description: Relative or absolute URL path for accessing or displaying the attachment in the web interface. Used by frontend to create download links or embed images.

models.name: discussion_board_article_moderation_history
models.description:
Immutable audit trail recording all moderation decisions and actions on articles.

Captures point-in-time snapshots of moderator decisions including approvals (with optional notes), rejections (with reasoning), edits, deletions, pinning, locking, and archival. Each record documents the moderator responsible, decision timestamp, action type, and associated context. Supports compliance requirements and enables moderator accountability tracking.

Records are append-only and never modified after creation. Retention is indefinite for complete historical tracking. Multiple records per article document the complete moderation lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Article being moderated. References {@link discussion_board_articles.id}. Links moderation action to specific article.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator performing the action. References {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}. Records who made the moderation decision.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of moderation action performed. Valid values: approved (published for public viewing), rejected (declined for publication), edited (content modified for compliance), deleted (removed from system), pinned (featured at top), locked (disabled comments), archived (hidden from listings). Determines what contextual data is stored.

plainFields.name: action_timestamp
plainFields.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when moderation action was performed. Immutable after creation. Used to establish chronological order of all moderation events.

plainFields.name: approval_notes
plainFields.description: Optional feedback provided by moderator during approval decision. Maximum 1,000 characters. Visible to contributor and other moderators. Null for non-approval actions.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Explanation for article rejection decision provided by moderator. Maximum 500 characters. Helps contributor understand how to revise for resubmission. Null for non-rejection actions.

plainFields.name: removal_reason
plainFields.description: Explanation for deletion or archival action. Maximum 500 characters. Provides context for why published article was removed from public access. Null for other action types.

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
User comments posted on published articles enabling discussion and community interaction.

Each comment represents a user contribution to a discussion thread on a specific article. Comments support hierarchical threading where users can reply to the article (top-level comment) or reply to other comments (nested reply), creating organized conversation threads. Comments are published immediately upon submission without requiring moderator approval, though moderators retain the ability to edit or remove inappropriate comments.

Comments maintain a complete audit trail including creation timestamp, modification tracking, author information, and deletion status. The system supports soft deletion, allowing threads to maintain context even after comments are removed by authors or moderators. This design preserves the coherence of discussion threads while respecting user privacy and moderation needs.

Comments include optional file attachments (images only) to enable contributors to share supporting visual content. Attachments are tracked separately for efficient management and access control.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: The article this comment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_contributor_id
foreignFields.description: The contributor who posted this comment. {@link discussion_board_contributors.id}.

foreignFields.name: parent_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Parent comment ID if this is a reply to another comment. Null for top-level comments on the article. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The comment text content. Required field containing the discussion contribution. Minimum 1 character, maximum 5,000 characters per specification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the comment was created. Recorded at the moment the comment is posted by the contributor.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent modification. Updated when the comment is edited by the author or moderator. Starts equal to created_at.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: ISO 8601 timestamp if comment was deleted by author or moderator. Null for active comments. Used for soft deletion to preserve thread structure.

plainFields.name: is_deleted
plainFields.description: Whether this comment has been deleted and is no longer visible. True indicates soft delete; false indicates active comment. Used for quick filtering of active comments.

plainFields.name: edit_count
plainFields.description: Number of times this comment has been edited by the author or moderator. Starts at 0 when comment is created. Incremented with each modification. Helps track comment history.

plainFields.name: reply_count
plainFields.description: Number of direct replies to this comment. Used for efficiently displaying reply count without querying child comments. Updated whenever a reply is added or removed.

plainFields.name: article_publication_status
plainFields.description: Cached publication status of the parent article at the time the comment was posted (e.g., 'published', 'archived'). Immutable record providing audit context for when comment was created.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_attachments
models.description:
Image file attachments associated with comments to support visual evidence and discussion context.

Comments support optional file attachments limited to images (JPG, PNG, GIF formats) to enable contributors to share visual supporting materials within their discussion contributions. Each comment can have up to 2 image attachments with individual file size limits of 5MB. Attachments are stored with unique identifiers to prevent filename collisions and provide secure file management.

Each attachment record maintains metadata including the original filename for user display, file type for validation, file size for storage management, upload timestamp for audit purposes, and the contributor ID of the uploader for accountability. The system tracks attachment storage location and MIME type for proper browser handling and content delivery.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment this attachment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_contributor_id
foreignFields.description: The contributor who uploaded this attachment. {@link discussion_board_contributors.id}.

plainFields.name: original_file_name
plainFields.description: Original filename as uploaded by the contributor. User-visible name displayed in the attachment list. Between 1-255 characters to accommodate typical filename lengths.

plainFields.name: file_type
plainFields.description: File extension in lowercase indicating the file format (e.g., 'jpg', 'png', 'gif'). Used for validation against allowed types. Images only per specification.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of the file in bytes. Used for validating upload limits (max 5MB for comment images) and tracking storage usage.

plainFields.name: uploaded_at
plainFields.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the attachment was uploaded. Recorded at the moment the file is accepted and stored.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the file for proper browser display and content delivery (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/gif'). Used to set correct HTTP Content-Type headers.

plainFields.name: display_url
plainFields.description: URL path or absolute URL for accessing or displaying the attachment in the web interface. Relative or absolute path depending on file storage implementation.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_moderation_history
models.description:
Immutable audit trail recording all moderator actions on comments for accountability and compliance.

This table maintains a complete and permanent record of every moderation action taken on comments, including edits and removals. The moderation history serves as an immutable audit log that documents when comments were modified by moderators, who performed the actions, and what actions were taken. This supports platform accountability, moderator oversight, and compliance with content governance policies.

Each history entry captures the moderator who performed the action, the exact timestamp, the type of action taken (edit or removal), and optional reason text explaining the moderation decision. The table is append-only; records are never deleted or modified, preserving the integrity of the historical record. This design enables complete traceability of all moderation decisions and supports dispute resolution if contributors appeal moderation actions.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment that was moderated. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: The moderator who performed the moderation action. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of moderation action performed on the comment. Valid values: 'edited' (moderator edited comment content), 'removed' (moderator deleted the comment). Indicates what moderation measure was taken.

plainFields.name: action_timestamp
plainFields.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the moderation action was performed. Recorded at the moment the moderator submits their action. Critical for audit trail chronology.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Optional text explanation provided by the moderator documenting why the action was taken. Maximum 500 characters. May include guideline reference or specific violation explanation. Null if no reason was provided.

plainFields.name: comment_content_before
plainFields.description: The original comment content before the moderation action was taken. Preserved for audit purposes to show what was edited or removed. Full text stored to maintain complete record.

plainFields.name: comment_content_after
plainFields.description: The comment content after the moderation action. For 'edited' actions, shows the new moderated content. For 'removed' actions, empty string or null indicating deletion. Used to track what changes were made.

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_queue
models.description:
Tracks articles awaiting moderator review in the approval workflow.

This table represents the moderation queue that stores all articles submitted by contributors awaiting moderator approval. Each queue entry corresponds to an article in pending_approval status and captures the submission context, moderator assignment, and review metadata.

When a contributor submits an article, a queue entry is created automatically. Moderators review articles in queue order (oldest submissions first) and remove entries upon approval or rejection. The queue table enables efficient workflow management and ensures no articles slip through without review.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article awaiting review. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_contributor_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the contributor who submitted the article. {@link discussion_board_contributors.id}

foreignFields.name: assigned_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to moderator assigned to review this article, if any. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was submitted for review. Used for queue ordering.

plainFields.name: review_started_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when a moderator began reviewing the article, null if not yet reviewed.

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description: Priority level for review: 'normal' (default), 'high' (flagged for expedited review), 'low' (secondary priority). Guides moderator workflow prioritization.

plainFields.name: submission_notes
plainFields.description: Optional notes from contributor explaining the article or addressing previous feedback. Maximum 1000 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the queue entry was created (same as submitted_at).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent update to this queue entry.

models.name: discussion_board_user_suspensions
models.description:
Tracks suspension and restriction actions against contributor accounts.

This table maintains a complete history of account suspensions and restrictions imposed on contributors by moderators for policy violations. Each suspension record captures enforcement context, duration, and resolution, enabling tracking of account status across the suspension lifecycle.

When a moderator determines a contributor has repeatedly violated policies or committed severe violations, a suspension record is created. Suspensions have defined durations (7 days, 30 days, permanent) and are tracked with status transitions. This table enables the moderation system to enforce account restrictions and moderators to review enforcement history.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_contributor_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the contributor whose account is suspended. {@link discussion_board_contributors.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the moderator who issued the suspension. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}

plainFields.name: suspension_type
plainFields.description: Type of suspension: 'posting_restriction' (cannot post articles/comments for duration), 'account_suspension' (cannot login), 'permanent_ban' (account permanently disabled). Determines enforcement mechanism.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation for the suspension action. Maximum 1000 characters. Includes specific violations that led to suspension.

plainFields.name: severity_level
plainFields.description: Severity classification: 'minor' (first offense, light restriction), 'moderate' (second offense, extended restriction), 'severe' (repeated violations or serious single violation), 'permanent' (irreversible account ban).

plainFields.name: duration_days
plainFields.description: Duration of suspension in days. Null for permanent suspensions. Used to calculate expiration_at.

plainFields.name: suspended_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the suspension became effective.

plainFields.name: expiration_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the suspension expires and account restrictions are automatically lifted. Null for permanent suspensions.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current suspension status: 'active' (suspension in effect), 'lifted' (moderator manually lifted the suspension), 'expired' (suspension duration completed). Determines whether restrictions apply.

plainFields.name: lifted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the suspension was manually lifted by a moderator. Null if not yet lifted or suspension expired naturally.

plainFields.name: lift_reason
plainFields.description: Explanation for why the suspension was lifted. Maximum 500 characters. Null if suspension not yet lifted.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the suspension record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent update to the suspension record.

models.name: discussion_board_content_violation_records
models.description:
Documents specific content violations detected in articles and comments.

This table maintains detailed records of individual content policy violations found in articles and comments. Each violation record captures what was violated, why it violated the policy, the severity, and the moderator action taken to resolve it.

When moderators identify content that violates community guidelines (during article review or comment monitoring), a violation record is created. These records enable violation tracking per contributor, inform decisions about escalating restrictions, and provide audit trail of enforcement actions. Violation history directly informs suspension decisions through accumulation of violations within time windows.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_contributor_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the contributor who created the violating content. {@link discussion_board_contributors.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article containing the violation, if violation is in an article. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}. Exactly one of article_id or comment_id must be non-null; constraint enforced by application validation.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the comment containing the violation, if violation is in a comment. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}. Exactly one of article_id or comment_id must be non-null; constraint enforced by application validation.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the moderator who documented this violation. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}

plainFields.name: violation_type
plainFields.description: Specific type of violation: 'hate_speech' (targeting protected groups), 'personal_attack' (attacking individuals), 'misinformation' (false claims), 'harassment' (coordinated or repeated targeting), 'spam' (promotional content), 'off_topic' (unrelated to discussion), 'graphic_content' (explicit imagery/violence), 'threats' (violence or harm threats), 'copyright' (copyright violations), 'other' (other policy violations).

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Severity classification: 'minor' (small issues, correctable by editing), 'moderate' (clear violation, requires action), 'severe' (serious violation like hate speech or threats). Determines enforcement response.

plainFields.name: violation_description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of what was violated and why. Includes specific examples from content that violated the policy. Maximum 2000 characters.

plainFields.name: action_taken
plainFields.description: Enforcement action: 'edited' (moderator edited content to comply), 'removed' (content deleted), 'warned' (warning issued to user), 'restricted' (user posting restricted), 'suspended' (account suspended), 'reported_to_admin' (escalated to administrator). Describes what moderator did in response.

plainFields.name: action_details
plainFields.description: Additional details about the action taken. If content was edited, what was changed. If user warned/restricted, what was the specific message. Maximum 1000 characters.

plainFields.name: detected_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the violation was detected by moderator or automated system.

plainFields.name: content_snapshot
plainFields.description: Snapshot of the violating content at time of detection. First 500 characters of content for reference. Used to verify violation even if content later changed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the violation record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent update to the violation record.

models.name: discussion_board_moderator_audit_log
models.description:
Complete audit trail of all moderator actions for accountability and compliance.

This table maintains an immutable, append-only audit log of every action performed by moderators on the platform. Each log entry captures what action was taken, on what content, by which moderator, and when, creating a comprehensive accountability record.

The audit log enables moderation review, compliance audits, performance analysis of moderator decisions, and dispute resolution when users appeal moderation actions. Every moderator action (article approval/rejection, comment removal, user warning/suspension, edit, etc.) must be recorded here. The audit log is never modified after creation, only appended to, ensuring integrity and immutability of the record.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the moderator who performed the action. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article involved in the action, if applicable. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the comment involved in the action, if applicable. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

foreignFields.name: affected_contributor_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the contributor affected by the action (author of article/comment or user being restricted). {@link discussion_board_contributors.id}

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of action performed: 'article_approved' (article approved for publication), 'article_rejected' (article rejected from publication), 'article_edited' (moderator edited article content), 'article_deleted' (article removed), 'article_archived' (article archived), 'article_pinned' (article pinned to top), 'article_unpinned' (article unpinned), 'article_locked' (article locked from comments), 'article_unlocked' (article unlocked), 'comment_edited' (moderator edited comment), 'comment_removed' (comment deleted), 'user_warned' (warning issued), 'user_restricted' (posting restricted), 'user_suspended' (account suspended), 'user_unsuspended' (suspension lifted), 'violation_recorded' (violation documented).

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Explanation of why the action was taken. For rejections, the reason for rejection. For removals, the guideline violated. For restrictions, the reason for restriction. Maximum 1000 characters.

plainFields.name: old_status
plainFields.description: Previous state before action. For articles: old publication status. For users: old account status. Null if not applicable. Used to track state transitions.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: New state after action. For articles: new publication status. For users: new account status. Null if not applicable. Shows result of action.

plainFields.name: additional_metadata
plainFields.description: Additional contextual information about the action. For edits, what was changed. For suspensions, duration. For warnings, specific message. JSON formatted data. Maximum 2000 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the action was performed. This is the authoritative timestamp for the action occurrence.

models.name: mv_discussion_board_article_search_index
models.description:
Materialized view providing optimized full-text search index for rapid article discovery.

This computed table denormalizes article data to support efficient keyword searching across titles and content. Rather than performing expensive full-text searches directly on the main articles table, queries target this indexed view for sub-second response times even with thousands of articles.

The index includes article title, content preview, and searchable metadata organized for relevance ranking. Search queries matching article titles are ranked higher than content-only matches. The view is refreshed periodically (typically hourly) to keep search results current while maintaining query performance.

This materialized view supports the core search discovery requirement: users can find articles by keyword within 1 second, enabling the platform's content discovery mechanisms.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article being indexed for search. Links this search index entry to the source article in the main discussion_board_articles table. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title text optimized for search ranking. Title matches are weighted more heavily than content matches in search results.

plainFields.name: content_preview
plainFields.description: First 500 characters of article content, preprocessed and cleaned for full-text search. Enables snippet generation in search results. Application layer may truncate to 200 characters for article list display.

plainFields.name: search_tokens
plainFields.description: Preprocessed and normalized search tokens extracted from title and content. Includes lowercased, stemmed versions of keywords for fuzzy matching. Stored as space-separated tokens to support trigram-based search with PostgreSQL GIN indexes.

plainFields.name: author_name
plainFields.description: Article author's username, included for author-based search filtering (e.g., 'articles by username'). References the contributor or moderator who created the article.

plainFields.name: category
plainFields.description: Article category for search filtering. Valid categories: Economics, Politics, Policy, Trade, Markets, Regulation, International, Analysis, Opinion, Other Discussion.

plainFields.name: published_at
plainFields.description: Publication timestamp used for sorting search results by date. Enables 'sort by newest first' search feature and date range filtering. Null values excluded from search index (only published articles).

plainFields.name: comment_count
plainFields.description: Denormalized comment count for the article. Enables search result sorting by discussion activity (most-commented articles ranked higher). Updated when articles receive comments.

plainFields.name: is_pinned
plainFields.description: Whether article is pinned/featured by moderators. Pinned articles are displayed at top of search results and category listings to increase visibility of important discussions.

plainFields.name: last_updated
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this search index entry was last refreshed from the source article. Used to track view freshness and manage materialized view refresh scheduling. Typically refreshed hourly or on article publication.

models.name: mv_discussion_board_category_article_statistics
models.description:
Materialized view providing article count and activity statistics for each category.

This computed table aggregates statistics about articles in each category, enabling efficient category browsing without querying the main articles table. The view tracks total article count per category, provides category-level metadata, and supports rapid display of category options with article counts in the user interface.

When users browse the platform, they see category selections with article counts (e.g., 'Economics (247 articles)', 'Politics (189 articles)') without expensive aggregation queries. This view is refreshed periodically to reflect newly published articles while maintaining consistently fast category browsing performance.

The statistics support the discovery workflow: users quickly identify relevant categories and can confidently browse knowing activity levels in each topic area.

plainFields.name: category
plainFields.description: Article category name. One entry per category: Economics, Politics, Policy, Trade, Markets, Regulation, International, Analysis, Opinion, Other Discussion.

plainFields.name: article_count
plainFields.description: Total number of published articles in this category. Used to display counts next to category names in the browsing interface (e.g., 'Economics (247)').

plainFields.name: comment_count
plainFields.description: Total number of comments across all articles in this category. Indicates overall discussion activity level by category.

plainFields.name: last_article_published_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recently published article in this category. Helps users identify which categories have recent activity.

plainFields.name: average_comments_per_article
plainFields.description: Average number of comments per article in this category. Indicates how engaged the community is in discussing category topics (e.g., 3.5 comments per article indicates active discussion).

plainFields.name: pinned_article_count
plainFields.description: Number of pinned/featured articles in this category. Helps users see which categories have moderator-highlighted content.

plainFields.name: last_updated
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this statistics entry was last refreshed from source article data. Indicates freshness of the displayed statistics.
